title: Weak-Identification-Robust GENIUS Inference for Censored Survival Outcomes with Many Instruments
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; projected paper-score ceiling 6 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: The note proves a feasible zero-strength test, but its unrestricted p/n result has only one known genetic coordinate governing exposure, event, and censor laws; the other p-1 coordinates add noise, so it does not establish a broadly usable many-instrument procedure.
Its generic learner requires balanced finite W-cells, positive atom masses, and a restrictive growth budget, leaving continuous survival and unknown-index learning outside the delivered result.

The tail augmentation and deleted-diagonal weak-identification test build on published ingredients in Bu et al. and Mikusheva and Sun; the new combination is substantive but remains a specialized construction.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4, so the graded tier subfield is capped at incremental.

The stated phi(H, G-hat, Q-hat) replaces only g,G,Q in def:risk-tail-score and therefore retains the true M_j/lambda_j, but the proof switches to M-hat_j/lambda-hat_j; the displayed product-bias identity requires the latter and does not follow from the stated definition.
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery phase derived an observable censoring-orthogonal tail-martingale score, diagonal-free quadratic inference through zero strength, exact full-line inversion, a four-group finite-atom learner, and a confounded observational-equivalence witness. The field-tier claim collapsed because only one coordinate carries identifying signal while the remaining coordinates add variance, and the feasible learner remains confined to balanced finite cells; the panel therefore rated the sound surviving package incremental. A continuous-survival learner, unknown-index learning, finite-sample calibration, and the fitted-martingale correction to the product-drift statement remain open.
tldr: The finite-atom risk-set tail score is censoring-orthogonal, and a block cross-fitted diagonal-free quadratic gives high-rank Gaussian inference through exactly zero GENIUS strength. The four-group known-index construction now permits arbitrary bounded finite-atom event and censor laws conditional on \(A,Z_1\), including exposure-confounded event laws, for every joint \(n,p\to\infty\). A confounded zero-strength pair has the same observed law under two different structural effects.
gap: Existing censored GENIUS point-estimator theory requires diverging strength. Generic CAR transforms and nonlinear many-moment robust tests establish adjacent pieces, but the inspected theorems do not verify a growing-rank deleted-diagonal test of learned censored GENIUS scores with uniform calibration at a zero structural Jacobian.
fill: Prove the observed-data score drift, feasible high-rank quadratic null law on explicitly diverging-dimension slices, finite-cell learner rates, full-line inversion, and power without dividing by identification strength.
